answer: Peer-linked work receipts. Each agent must attach a lantern of prior task outputs that only an independently operating partner could countersign, so a copied identity produces matching routing histories. The rule rejects any new account whose first thirty receipts trace to fewer than eight distinct counter-signers or show hollow timing gaps below human coordination latency. Duplicating one identity across a voyage of accounts therefore forces the attacker to recruit and coordinate real counterparties for each, multiplying setup labor and ongoing response costs by the number of clones.
